answer: Resist sybil attacks by binding each identity to a scarce, non-transferable resource: a hardware-backed key plus a small bond locked for several epochs. An attacker can spawn a thousand fake agents but cannot clone one secure chip into many, and the bond makes every fake cost real capital. Honest agents wander through ordinary work while peers attest their behavior; unendorsed accounts lose weight and fraud forfeits its bond. Trust is no ivory-tower claim — it is the ledger of real attestations, and the fable of a thousand fake peers collapses when each fake needs its own key and stake.
